messages.subject: Annotation of methylKit results with bed12 and genomation
parts:
Hi Altuna,

I have a question about genomation and the file format. I attached here a snippet of the input file I'm using. The problem is that genomation starts to read the table fine with "readTranscriptFeatures" command, but then soon fails at the step for intons. It works fine for the example files. Below is what I ran. I think there is something wrong with the formatting of the bed12 but I cannot figure out what.

Best,
Heidi

>gene.obj=readTranscriptFeatures("~/Documents/Great tit project/NCBI_NIOO GT Sequences/Reference_v1.1/ParusM_1.1_PrimAssembly/PA_ref_Parus_major1.1_top_level_12format.bed")
Reading the table...
Calculating intron coordinates...
Error in convertBed2Introns(bed) : this is not a valid bed file
>


> traceback
function (x = NULL, max.lines = getOption("deparse.max.lines"))
{
    n <- length(x <- .traceback(x))
    if (n == 0L)
        cat(gettext("No traceback available"), "\n")
    else {
        for (i in 1L:n) {
            xi <- x[[i]]
            label <- paste0(n - i + 1L, ": ")
            m <- length(xi)
            srcloc <- if (!is.null(srcref <- attr(xi, "srcref"))) {
                srcfile <- attr(srcref, "srcfile")
                paste0(" at ", basename(srcfile$filename), "#",
                  srcref[1L])
            }
            if (is.numeric(max.lines) && max.lines > 0L && max.lines <
                m) {
                xi <- c(xi[seq_len(max.lines)], " ...")
                m <- length(xi)
            }
            if (!is.null(srcloc)) {
                xi[m] <- paste0(xi[m], srcloc)
            }
            if (m > 1)
                label <- c(label, rep(substr("          ", 1L,
                  nchar(label, type = "w")), m - 1L))
            cat(paste0(label, xi), sep = "\n")
        }
    }
    invisible(x)
}

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Annotation of methylKit results with bed12 and genomation
parts:
Hi,
The function looks for "chr" string in the beginning of chromosome names. We might remove this requirement at some point, but for now your chromosome names must start with "chr" string.
https://github.com/Bioconductor-mirror/genomation/blob/master/R/readAnnotate.R#L101

Best
Altuna

Hi,

Just an update on my previous question and for other people who might come across the same issue. For me genomatio was able to read the gff file in fine as long as the first chromosome in the chrom-column had chr in the name it was able to read the following non-chr named chromosomes as well without an error.

Heidi
